card.name: Rebuttal of a just-stated claim
card.fires_on: Pronouns like This, That, they, or is right after a myth, misconception, or belief has been stated, just before the text calls it untrue or wrong. Also fires weakly on scattered other words in general web text.

modes.label: Pointing back at a myth
modes.description: A demonstrative or linking word that begins a reply to a claim just stated, such as a myth or misconception.
modes.example: This article explains some common misconceptions about lightning. For example, one misconception is that lightning never strikes the same place twice. This<< is>> untrue.

modes.label: Design list noun
modes.description: A noun inside a list of design constraints in educational text.
modes.example: (e.g., cost, time, trade-offs, properties of<< materials>>, safety and aesthetics)

card.writes: It lowers words about exaggeration and paranoia, so the pole seems to steer toward a plain statement that the claim is wrong.
card.plain: It fires where a text has just repeated a false belief and is about to say that it is wrong.
